name: DocVQA
description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images. Questions are categorized based on their reasoning requirements, including questions about forms, tables, layouts, handwritten text, photographs, figures, and running text.

creator.name: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
creator.affiliation: CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India; Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain

citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV] 5 Jan 2021
rai:dataCollection: Document images are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library. Images were downloaded from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset. Majority of documents in the library are binarized. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages which only have running text. Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from UCSF Industry Documents Library. The final set of images in the dataset are drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018. Documents include typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text from 5 major industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1900 to 2018, with most documents from the 1960-2000 period
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: OCR tokens are extracted using a commercial OCR application. For BERT QA models, OCR tokens recognized on document images are serialized to a single string, separated by space, in top-left to bottom-right order. To approximate answer spans, the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string is found.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation process was organized in three stages. Stage 1: Workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it. Workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question where warranted. Workers were instructed to ask questions which can be answered using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. Stage 2: A worker was shown an image and questions defined on it in the first stage (but not the answers), and was required to enter answers for the questions and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag questions if they found them inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity. Stage 3: If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the question is sent for review. The reviewer either accepts the question-answer (after editing if necessary) or ignores it. The third stage review is done by the authors themselves.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions flagged during the second stage due to language issues or ambiguity are not included in the dataset. Questions where answers from stage 1 and stage 2 do not match are reviewed in stage 3 by the authors.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple ground truth answers per question are collected where warranted. Questions are verified by a second annotator in stage 2.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers. Human performance measured using volunteers from the authors' institution.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR application used for extracting OCR tokens from document images
rai:dataBiases: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken a toll on the image quality. The authors tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA. Most documents are from food and nutrition related collections as they have a good number of non-binarized images.
rai:dataLimitations: Poor image quality due to binarization in some cases. OCR errors impact model performance. Models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding structure of the document is crucial. Large performance gap compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy). Models perform poorly on questions requiring understanding of figures and text on photographs, and on handwritten text recognition.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio to train, validation and test splits. Training: 39,463 questions and 10,194 images. Validation: 5,349 questions and 1,286 images. Testing: 5,188 questions and 1,287 images. The dataset is designed for Visual Question Answering on document images, modeled as an extractive QA problem where answers are extracted verbatim from the document.
